title: Priority spin-down telemetry collector and quiet handshake
author: Priya Desai
release_notes: Adds a low-traffic telemetry collector and a quiet-handshake mode to reduce noisy on-call wakeups during service spin-downs; includes a rollout plan and opt-in flag.
description:
Motivation: on low-traffic windows we observed a spike in noisy alerts during scale-down events. Signals caused by transient cold starts and aggressive alert thresholds were producing false-positive wakeups for on-call. This PR implements a lightweight priority spin-down telemetry collector plus a 'quiet-handshake' mode that: 1) captures ephemeral telemetry around scheduled scale-downs in a micro-batched in-memory buffer, 2) computes a compact prioritized signal summary (top-k root causes + confidence), and 3) performs a non-invasive quiet-handshake with the incident-bot before firing high-urgency pages. The handshake defers non-critical pages for a short jitter window and attaches the summarized snapshot to any page that proceeds.

What changed (high level): implemented a new collector service module (slo_toolkit/telemetry/spin_down_collector.py), added a quiet-handshake controller that talks to incident-bot via the existing triage API, added sampling and probabilistic backoff logic to avoid amplification, exposed a runtime feature flag (SLO_QUIET_HANDSHAKE) and a CLI toggle, added unit and integration tests, updated observability dashboards and doc pages.

Design details: the collector uses a bounded ring buffer to avoid noisy I/O during spin-downs; it supports per-service priority buckets (P0..P3) and computes a compact JSON-lite summary that contains a short hypothesis list, an event histogram, and a small metadata snapshot (commit, region, instance types). The quiet-handshake is intentionally conservative: it runs an enrichment pass (30-200ms) then calls incident-bot/triage with a 'quiet-probe' request. incident-bot replies with an advisory score; only advisories above threshold immediately escalate. Advisory below threshold are recorded and the system schedules a delayed re-eval (jittered up to 2m). This reduces noisy pages while ensuring true incidents still surface.

Testing & Validation: unit tests for ring buffer, sampling, summary generator; integration test that runs a simulated spin-down with synthetic telemetry; e2e that verifies a page is suppressed, advisory recorded, and that suppressed events are visible in the compact snapshot UI. Load tested with a synthetic workload generator to ensure the collector holds at <5% CPU overhead for service with 100 req/sec during spin-up/down cycles.

Rollout plan: feature gated off by default. Staged rollout: opt-in to 5% of customers -> monitor suppressed page rate and missed-detection telemetry -> 25% -> 100% with opt-out via runtime flag. Canary dashboard and alerting added: slo_toolkit/ops/dashboards/quiet_handshake_canary.json.

Related tickets: ENG-7422 (telemetry noise analysis), ENG-7581 (incident-bot triage API extension). See design note: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-7422/spin-down-telemetry-prioritization (internal link).
